I'm running this from inside the eslint project.  I don't have ESLint installed globally, and with the `eslint-plugin-markdown` that I'm using, I've had to install eslint within eslint (which I do with an `npm link` and `npm link eslint`).  It's a little unorthodox, I know, but it was working just fine.  I could also have done:

```
DEBUG=eslint* node bin/eslint.js --plugin markdown --no-eslintrc --config conf/rule-doc-config.json docs/rules/quote-props.md            
  eslint:cli Running on files +0ms
  eslint:config Using command line config conf/rule-doc-config.json +3ms

  0:0  warning  File ignored because of your .eslintignore file. Use --no-ignore to override

✖ 1 problem (0 errors, 1 warning)
```

There is no eslintignore path being specified, so I'm not sure what you mean there.
This looks like a bug. On top of that, we should decorate code that loads `.eslintignore` with debug statements, so we could trace them.
@BYK Do you think you could take a look at this?  It seems you made quite a few changes to the ignore logic when you implemented globs.
@IanVS Can you share the content of `.eslintignore` . thanks
There's not one.  I'm linting the eslint rule docs, from inside of the eslint project.

Here is the answer, Because by default eslint looks for file with extensions `.js`. 
Now if you say `--ext .md` then it would work fine.

Previously, if you specified a full filename, it would be linted no matter the extension, which I believe is correct.  The `--ext` flag should only be needed when you are providing a directory to search, IMHO.
@ianvs is correct - we should lint anything that is passed explicitly on the command line.

issue.body:
**What issue does this pull request address?**
#4828

**What changes did you make? (Give an overview)**
The main change here is to set an option on node_glob to return dotfiles from glob patterns (anything other than explicitly passed files).   In order for dotfiles to actually be linted, though, a negating ignore pattern like `!.*` will need to be used to override the default ignore behavior.

This turned out to be a bit more involved than just returning hidden files from our glob patterns.  That's because we were _not_ ignoring dotfiles by default in all cases, only when an `options` object was provided to `listFilesToProcess`, which was nearly always.  Except, it turns out, in the test `"should not return hidden files for standard glob patterns"`.  That _was_ okay, because globs would never return dotfiles, but that started failing as soon as I made the core change in this PR.  

Now that the glob pattern will include hidden files, we need to apply the default ignore rules.  _However_, we also want to _not_ ignore dotfiles if they are explicitly included in the glob pattern.  The only way I could find to solve this problem was to directly check the glob pattern with a regex to see if it includes hidden files.  If so, dotfiles are not ignored, and otherwise they are.

**Is there anything you'd like reviewers to focus on?**
Please give my regex a sanity check.  I tried to test it out and it seems to work, but I'm not super-confident in my regex skills.

I would also be happy to include any other tests that anyone thinks might be useful.
